summary: The transplant is faithful and the one outstanding finding landed. I diffed D-102 against the frozen D-101 turn-3 subject: every byte of the measurement contract — the path/digest identity bullets, both numbered launch sequences, the paired 10% formula, thin-only scope, preflight, and both target-process protocols — is identical, and the changes are confined to the protocol header, the disposition table, the D-101-to-D-102 identifier substitutions in the file-08 writes and Alternatives, the reversibility line, and the dispatch table. ADV-D101-T3-01 is the only thing that had to move, and it moved exactly where it should: the phrase 'immediately before each timed launch' is gone from the file (grep count 0), and the replacement row — inode-only stat after purge immediately before the cold launch and before an unpurged doctor launch, no stat or hash inside the cold/warm pair — is what both numbered sequences actually say. That matches COORD's own record of Codex's position (disposition row vs cold-only sequence) and D-101's 'a later new cycle (not turn 4) may retry', so the cycle is lawful. The whole attack list sweeps clean: no hash between purge and cold; sysctl.proc_cputype is rejected, not used; process arch is observed on the target and the image is thin-only; weekly rolls explicitly do not suppress the 10% rule; warm p50 is telemetry that cannot fail qualification; D-006's numerals stand exactly (cold p50/p95/p99 and warm p95/p99 are the five operative quantities, RSS 40/50 and 60/100); nothing claims QUALIFIED or SATISFIED; no implementation authorization and no condition-5 flip. All seven cited digests re-measure byte-exact, the D-101 predecessor commit exists, and no frozen D-101 or D-099 subject is modified in git. I simulated all five file-08 edits in a scratch copy: each anchor occurs exactly once, and afterwards PARTLY MET, '16 of 18', 'D-006 machine pins owed' and 'D-006-conforming successor' all fall to zero with no stale residue, the condition-4 row ends '| **MET** |', and G03/G04 keep OPEN/SPECIFIED with no SATISFIED. I have one SHOULD-FIX, and it is new. Re-running the macOS protocol against MacOSX15.4.sdk this cycle rather than carrying my D-101 measurement forward, I hit a call form I did not hit last time: posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np with a NULL subpref returns EINVAL and sets no preference at all, and the subsequent posix_spawn then succeeds with no architecture constraint. Step 1 specifies no reject path for the arch-request itself, so one of step 5's five conjuncts can silently become a no-op in a protocol that specifies an explicit reject for every other observation. Soundness survives — thin-only preflight, E matching the class, D0, proc_pidpath and P_TRANSLATED still determine the ISA on their own — which is why this is SHOULD-FIX and not MUST-FIX, but it is a fail-open seam in the one derivation this entry leans on hardest, and it is a one-clause fix.

objections.title: macOS step 1 has no reject path for the arch-preference request; step 5's spawn conjunct can silently be a no-op
objections.detail: Step 1 requires posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np 'to exactly one CPU type' and closes with 'Spawn failure -> reject'. That reject covers posix_spawn. It does not cover posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np itself, and the entry says nothing about the subtype argument. Measured against MacOSX15.4.sdk on this host: called with count=1, pref={CPU_TYPE_X86_64} and subpref=NULL — a natural reading of 'exactly one CPU type', and the shape of the older sibling posix_spawnattr_setbinpref_np, which takes no subtype at all — the call returns EINVAL (22) with ocount=0 and sets no preference; the following posix_spawn of the thin arm64 image then succeeds rc=0 with P_TRANSLATED=0. The mirrored case behaves the same. Passed subpref={CPU_SUBTYPE_ANY} instead, the call returns 0 with ocount=1 and the mismatched spawns fail rc=86 EBADARCH in both directions, which is the behaviour the entry assumes. So the difference between an enforcing arch request and no arch request at all is an unchecked return value on an argument the entry never mentions. This matters because step 5 lists 'step 1 requested exactly that CPU type and spawn succeeded, so any other ISA is unspawnable' as one of five conjuncts that together substitute for the per-process CPU-type API the entry correctly establishes does not exist on this SDK. Two things weaken that conjunct. First, the silent-EINVAL path above, with no reject clause — conspicuous in a protocol that is otherwise exhaustive about reject paths ('Unreadable -> reject', 'If n != PROC_PIDTBSDINFO_SIZE, reject', 'Missing type, unreadable pointer, no NUL inside 32 bytes, or a failed read -> reject'). The man page does not help an implementer here: it documents EINVAL only for an invalid attr, so the NULL-subpref failure is undocumented. Second, the man page scopes the EBADARCH-on-no-match semantics to Universal binaries ('When spawn(2) ... is subsequently invoked on a Universal binary ... If there is no match, then the attempt to create the child process will fail with the error EBADARCH'), while this entry's thin-only scope guarantees P is never universal. Thin-image enforcement is measured true on this host but sits outside the documented contract, so a future kernel treating an inapplicable preference as a no-op would drop the conjunct the same silent way. Direction of failure, stated plainly: this does not admit wrong-ISA evidence today. For a thin image on a class-matched host the surviving conjuncts are sufficient on their own — preflight item 2 rejects any image with more than one slice, E must match the class, D0 pins the bytes, proc_pidpath must equal P, and P_TRANSLATED=0 excludes Rosetta. That is why I file SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX. But the entry states the spawn conjunct as load-bearing, and as written a conforming implementation can lose it without anything rejecting. Fix, one clause in step 1: require posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np to be called with subpref={CPU_SUBTYPE_ANY} and to return 0 with ocount == 1; non-zero return or ocount != 1 -> reject. Optionally add that thin-image enforcement is measured on host rather than documented, so the conjunct is corroborative and the derivation does not rest on it. Disclosure: these bytes are identical to D-101 turn 3, where I filed CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. I missed this then because my probe happened to use the correct call form on the first attempt and I never exercised the NULL-subpref path. D-102 is a new cycle and this file's own bytes carry the contract, so I file it now rather than let a prior consent stand in for a measurement I had not made.
objections.measured: subpref=NULL: setarchpref rc=22 (EINVAL) ocount=0, then posix_spawn rc=0 — thin arm64 img requested as CPU_TYPE_X86_64 ran with P_TRANSLATED=0; thin x86_64 img requested as CPU_TYPE_ARM64 ran with P_TRANSLATED=1. subpref={CPU_SUBTYPE_ANY}: setarchpref rc=0 ocount=1, matched spawns rc=0, both mismatched spawns rc=86 EBADARCH. MacOSX15.4.sdk, clang -arch arm64, /tmp/d102/m.
objections.proposedFix: In macOS step 1, after naming the CPU type: 'The call passes subtype CPU_SUBTYPE_ANY and must return 0 with ocount == 1; a non-zero return or ocount != 1 -> reject.'

notesNonBlocking.title: At N=21 nearest-rank, p99 is the maximum sample, so both the absolute p99 gate and its paired ratio rest on one extreme order statistic
notesNonBlocking.detail: The estimator gives rank = ceil(p x 21) -> 11/20/21, which I re-checked. Rank 21 of 21 is the maximum. So D-006's cold p99 <= 250 ms bound is applied to the single slowest accepted job, and the paired formula's candidate_p99 / previous_p99 is a ratio of two maxima. That is high-variance in both directions: one unlucky candidate outlier fails the gate, and one unlucky previous outlier inflates the denominator and lets a real regression pass. The entry's choice of N=21 is deliberate and correct in its own terms — it is what makes p95 and p99 land on distinct ranks, which was the D-094 defect — and D-006 requires p99 bounded, so any small N forces p99 onto the maximum. Raising N is the only thing that separates them, and N is a cost decision this entry is entitled to make. Recording the property so it is a known consequence rather than a later surprise at the first paired qualification. Not blocking and not a defect.

objectionNote: OBJECTIONS. 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 3 NOTE. The transplant is faithful, ADV-D101-T3-01 is genuinely landed, the file-08 edits apply cleanly with no stale residue, and every item on the attack list sweeps clean. The single SHOULD-FIX is new this cycle and came from re-measuring rather than re-reading: macOS step 1 specifies no reject path for posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np itself, and with a NULL subpref that call fails EINVAL, sets no preference, and lets the spawn proceed unconstrained — so one of step 5's five conjuncts can silently become a no-op. The derivation stays sound because thin-only preflight, the E match, D0, proc_pidpath and P_TRANSLATED carry it alone, which is why this is SHOULD-FIX; but the entry states that conjunct as load-bearing and specifies an explicit reject for every other observation it makes, so this one should get the same clause. One sentence in step 1 closes it. I consented to byte-identical text at D-101 turn 3 and did not catch this then; I am not letting that consent stand in for a measurement I had not made.
